# Physiology, Islets of Langerhans

**Authors:** Zainab Shahid, Gurdeep Singh

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

The islets of Langerhans are clusters of pancreatic cells discovered by Dr. Paul Langerhans, a pathologist who also discovered the dendritic Langerhans cells in 1869. Each islet contains up to a few thousand endocrine cells, and the islets constitute up to 2% of the total pancreatic mass. The islet cells include the alpha cells, beta cells, delta cells, epsilon cells, and pancreatic polypeptide (PP) cells, and each cell releases a specific hormone in response to signals.
